notes:
Summary: FireTrail builds low-latency conversational and personalization engines for live multiplayer experiences (in-game chat, NPC dialogue, dynamic content). They're very latency- and cost-sensitive — small latency regressions are highly visible in UX.

Quick background / objectives:
- POC started Nov 2025; goal: replace brittle in-house inference infra with a platform that provides consistent p95 latency <= 60ms for chat at 20-50 RPS while reducing token cost by at least 20% vs current baseline.
- Workloads: conversational chat (multi-turn, context window ~2k tokens), rapid embeddings for semantic lookup (hot cache + cold fallback), reranking for candidate responses.
- Model preference: open LLMs (quantized LLaMA-variant for on-prem) with fallback to smaller distilled model when load spikes. Interested in automated routing and graceful degradation.

Recent timeline / activity (CRM-style bullets):
- 2025-11-05: Initial discovery call (Ava) — product fit confirmed, high-level SLOs captured.
- 2025-12-03: Security questionnaire submitted; asked for SOC2 report and KMS integration details (drive:/FireTrail/Security_Request_Response.docx).
- 2026-01-09: Integration kickoff; engineering provided API keys and test harness. (gmail_thread_20260109_xyz)
- 2026-01-20: Basic connectivity + sample chat flow done. First micro-batching tests run against hosted endpoint — p95 ~70-85ms (non-optimized).
- 2026-02-10: Local Triton baseline (self-hosted) ran: p95 65-90ms depending on sequence length; cost estimate high.
- 2026-02-15: Deep-dive with SE (Rohan) and infra leads (fireflies ff_20260215_8492) — discussed batching, KV/prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs and routing policies.
- 2026-02-24: Redwood provided sample Optimize config (batching/caching knobs + suggested quantization levels). Micro-benchmarks with Redwood settings show p95 improvement to ~50-60ms with 8-bit quantization on dedicated GPUs.
- 2026-03-01: Redwood SE and FireTrail devs agreed to run a full perf benchmark (end-to-end, 24-hour ramp) and produce cost/latency S-curve. Benchmark window targeted 2026-03-04.

Key technical requirements / acceptance criteria (as stated by FireTrail CTO):
- Latency: p95 chat latency <= 60ms at steady-state 30 RPS with 2k context window; spike performance: graceful degradation to smaller model <150ms.
- Throughput: embeddings subsystem must support 400-800 QPS with 30ms median.
- Cost: target total hosting cost reduction >= 20% vs current infra for 1M monthly active users (pooled estimate).
- Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route p95 histograms, KV cache hit rate, per-request trace linking to game session id.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 report provided, SSO/SAML, KMS integration for keys, audit logs retained 90 days, data residency in NA/EU options.

Interest areas (explicit asks):
- Optimize -> recommendations: ideal batch size distribution for their request pattern; prefix/KV cache settings for multi-turn chat; quantization profiles (8-bit vs 4-bit) and expected quality delta.
- Perf benchmarking requests: Redwood to run synthetic and replay-based benchmarks using FireTrail production traces (redacted); include p50/p95/p99 and cost per 100k tokens.
- Routing and fallback: want to test automatic fallback to low-cost variant during sustained load and A/B rollouts for model upgrades.

Quotes / verbatim: "We need sub-60ms p95 for in-game chat — anything higher causes noticeable lag and player churn." — CTO (call 2026-02-15)

Decisions to be made / procurement notes:
- Procurement needs a vendor security pack + pricing deck for dedicated capacity; legal requires data residency and SLA language. (drive:/FireTrail/Redwood_PoC_Pricing_v1.pdf)
- Internal budget committee meets 2026-03-08 to approve expanded POC budget for dedicated nodes. Forecasted close if POC passes -> Apr 2026.

POC scope for benchmark run (requested to Redwood):
- 24-hour ramp: 5 -> 50 RPS with production-like interleaving of chat/embedding/rerank.
- Test matrix across: batching sizes, cache TTLs, quantization levels (8-bit, 4-bit), and dedicated vs hosted config.
- Deliverables: SLO heatmap, cost per 100k tokens, per-model quality regression notes, recommended config for production.

Next steps (explicit):
- Redwood to run full perf benchmark 2026-03-04; share results and Optimize recommendations by 2026-03-09.
- Exec review week of 2026-03-10 to decide commitment to Dedicated nodes.

Open questions / blockers:
- Legal/Procurement: precise wording for data residency and incident reporting in contract.
- SE: need replay traces anonymized (FireTrail to provide by 2026-03-02).
- Cost sign-off: POC expansion contingent on budget approval 2026-03-08.

Internal notes for AE/SE (short):
- Focus on concrete numbers in benchmark deliverable. FireTrail is metric-driven — latency and cost.
- Avoid vague QoE claims. Provide quantized model quality deltas (user-facing metrics) not just perplexity.
- Offer a short-term canary plan (2-node dedicated pool) as low-risk for procurement.
